rationale: Sprint 1's gate criteria all reproduce independently (context 34604 B, coord active 3678 B, core-cap check rc 0 at 54/60 and 89/100, workflow default execution, baseline JSON present, Stop hook registered, autoprune gone) and all sprint-owned bats suites are green, so the sprint's headline result stands. But three of the nineteen reviewer findings reproduce as real defects introduced by this range: a duplicate archive-heading collision in mb-checklist-prune.sh that removes a checklist section from checklist.md without it ever reaching progress.md (I reproduced the loss on a two-section fixture) — that is a direct violation of AGR-043, the governing agreement of Stage 5, and falsifies Stage 5 DoD 'every removed block is found verbatim in progress.md'; an unvalidated path join in the new mb-checklist-v2.py that lets an mb-plan marker read a file outside the bank (reproduced, leaked a heading from ../../secret/leak.md into checklist.md); and a 3-line change in mb-work-state-lib.sh that converts the fail-closed NOITEM verdict into NOFILE for an unparseable spec tasks.md, so `done` certifies unverified:no_declaration_surface where the contract in the same file (lines 76-82) says it must never certify. Each is a small, local fix. The other sixteen findings are backlog: they are either fail-safe by design, already filed (I-189/I-190), match the plan's stated contract verbatim, or are style/test-hygiene at WARNING level under AGR-030.

blocking_issues.message: [slice B, reviewer line 'mb-checklist-prune.sh:102'] Archive identity is `## [checklist archive] <TODAY> — <label>` and confirmation is a bare grep -qxF of that heading. Two archivable sections that share a label collide: the first is appended and confirmed, the second skips its append at line 105 because the heading already exists, still passes the line-109 confirmation, and is added to DROP_ARGS — so `apply --drop legacy:<heading>` removes BOTH sections while only the first body ever reached progress.md. Verified by reproduction: a checklist with two `### Closed work` sections (bodies 'FIRST BODY MARKER' / 'SECOND BODY MARKER') run through `mb-checklist-prune.sh --apply` left checklist.md empty and progress.md containing only the first body; `grep -c 'SECOND BODY MARKER' progress.md` = 0. This falsifies Stage 5 DoD ('каждый убранный блок найден в progress.md дословно') and violates AGR-043, the agreement Stage 5 exists to implement. The `.checklist.md.bak.<ts>` backup makes it recoverable, not prevented.
blocking_issues.fix: Make the archive identity collision-resistant (e.g. append the block's checklist line range or a content hash to the heading/key) and confirm the COMPLETE block body — not just the heading — is present in progress.md before adding its key to DROP_ARGS. Add a regression test with two same-label archivable sections asserting both bodies land in progress.md.

blocking_issues.message: [slice B, reviewer line 'mb-checklist-v2.py:47'] `_titles` joins the plan name parsed from `<!-- mb-plan:... -->` straight onto plans_dir (`plans_dir / name`, `plans_dir / 'done' / name`) with no basename or containment check, and `_is_closed` (line 55) does the same. Verified by reproduction: a checklist containing `<!-- mb-plan:../../secret/leak.md -->` made `mb-checklist-v2.py apply` read that out-of-bank file and render its `# ` heading ('top secret project title') as the block title in checklist.md. An absolute path or a symlink works the same way, and via `_is_closed` a crafted marker can also flip a live plan to 'closed' and move its block out of the live registry. This is the same class the project already treats as a blocker and already solved for the analogous locator — `resolve_spec_source` in scripts/mb-work-state-lib.sh:149-175 rejects separators, dot segments and traversal before any join (r3 review [2]).
blocking_issues.fix: Reject any marker value that is not a plain basename (no '/', no '..', no leading '.', not absolute) before joining, and resolve each candidate through a canonical-under-plans-dir check as resolve_spec_source does. Add a test asserting a traversal marker yields the fallback title and never opens a file outside plans_dir.

blocking_issues.message: [slice A, reviewer line 'mb-work-state-lib.sh:116'] The file IS in the sprint range — `git log --oneline 364164a..a18235b -- scripts/mb-work-state-lib.sh` returns 85e39bb, and the diff is exactly the 3 added lines at 116-118, so this is a defect introduced here, not out-of-scope. The guard skips any parsed source with no `task`-kind item, which is correct for a plan but also swallows a real spec whose tasks.md is empty or whose `<!-- mb-task:N -->` markers are mangled: it falls through to NOFILE instead of NOITEM. Verified by reproduction: with `<bank>/specs/demo/tasks.md` containing prose only, and again with it empty, `eval_declaration <bank> '' demo 1` prints NOFILE; a well-formed tasks.md asked for a missing item still correctly prints NOITEM. scripts/mb-work-state-eval.sh:121 maps NOFILE to MBW_DONE_GATE=unverified:no_declaration_surface and returns 0, so `done` certifies an item whose declaration surface is broken — exactly what lines 76-82 of this file, and the line-88 comment 'the binding is broken and must never certify', forbid. The source category ('spec'/'plan') is already available as the fifth argument (SRC_LEGACY / `source_` at mb-work-state-eval.sh:97), so the guard can be made kind-aware without new plumbing.
blocking_issues.fix: Gate the zero-task shortcut on the declared source kind: `continue` only when the source is a plan; for a spec source with a resolved-but-taskless file, emit NOITEM (or an explicit parse-error verdict) so `done` still fails closed. Add a regression test for an empty and a marker-mangled spec tasks.md asserting `done` exits 5.

backlog_items.title: cost_report.py: marker regexes match any substring, so `cat pytest.ini` counts as a test run
backlog_items.rationale: [slice A, reviewer line 'cost_report.py:44'] Confirmed accurate: TEST_CMD_RE at line 43 and ITEM_OPEN_RE/ITEM_CLOSE_RE at lines 51-52 are unanchored, and tests/pytest/test_mb_cost_report.py:130 asserts ('cat pytest.ini', True) with the comment 'regex is substring-based — documented behavior'. Non-blocking: the line-41 comment freezes the pattern deliberately because the Sprint 2/3 gates cite baseline numbers measured with it, and Stage 1's DoD only requires the reported numbers to match the fixture, which they do. The cost is metric noise, not a user-visible bug. Any fix must re-measure the baseline or the Sprint 2/3 comparison stops being like-for-like.

backlog_items.title: mb-context.sh: checklist trimming drops ✅ lines individually, orphaning continuation lines in non-v2 checklists
backlog_items.rationale: [slice A, reviewer line 'mb-context.sh:0'] Line 120 is literally `kept = [ln for ln in lines if '✅' not in ln]`, so the reviewer's reading is right. Non-blocking: Stage 3's spec says exactly this ('checklist.md — сначала выбрасываются строки с ✅, затем хвост') and the bats contract is '✅ lines dropped before ⬜ lines'; with the v2 format this same sprint introduced (one line per stage) a line IS an item, so the two coincide today. The residue only affects legacy multi-line checklists, it is display-only (nothing is written back to disk), and the marker line plus --full point at the full file.

backlog_items.title: test_context_budget.bats mutates and rm -f's .mb-config inside the checked-in fixture dir
backlog_items.rationale: [slice A, reviewer line 'test_context_budget.bats:31'] Confirmed: teardown runs `rm -f "${FIXTURE:?}/.mb-config"` against tests/fixtures/context-budget/.memory-bank. Non-blocking: `git ls-files tests/fixtures/context-budget/` shows .mb-config is not tracked, so only a file the test itself creates is deleted — no checked-in state is at risk. The real cost is a race under parallel bats runs. Copy the fixture bank into TMPDIR_T in setup.

backlog_items.title: cost_report.py is 313 lines with five responsibilities (SRP split candidate)
backlog_items.rationale: [slice A, reviewer line 'cost_report.py:0'] Line count confirmed (313 in the diffstat). Non-blocking by project policy: AGR-030 states the 400-line limit is a guideline and the only mechanical check is SRP at 300 with severity WARNING, and explicitly says implementers must not reshape architecture to hit the number. Stage 1's own code rule ('SRP — парсинг отдельно от CLI') is met: parsing lives in memory_bank_skill/cost_report.py and the CLI in scripts/mb-cost-report.py.

backlog_items.title: mb-status-rotate.sh confirms archival by heading only; a stale identical heading can mask a silent no-append
backlog_items.rationale: [slice B, reviewer line 'mb-status-rotate.sh:136'] Confirmed: line 141 is `grep -qxF -- "$heading" "$PROGRESS"` where heading is only `## [status archive] <heading text>`, and mb-work-progress-append.sh is fail-safe (exits 0 without writing on lock timeout). Non-blocking, unlike its checklist sibling: reaching a lossy state needs a chain — a prior run that appended block N then aborted at line 144, the same section subsequently edited in status.md, AND a lock timeout on the retry — and line 149 writes `.status.md.bak.<ts>` before any rewrite, so status.md is recoverable. I could not construct a single-run reproduction. Harden it the same way as the checklist blocker.

backlog_items.title: mb-status-rotate.sh --keep N keeps the first N dated sections in file order, not the newest N by date
backlog_items.rationale: [slice B, reviewer line 'mb-status-rotate.sh:98'] The behaviour is real (line 100: `if seen_dated > keep`), but the reviewer's premise that newest-by-date is 'required' is wrong on two counts I checked. Stage 4's What-to-do says 'сверх первых N' — first N in file order — and the script header states it at line 9. And the convention is newest-first: `git show 364164a:.memory-bank/status.md` lists dated headings 2026-07-28, 07-18, 07-18, 07-17, 07-15, 07-15, 07-13, 07-06 in descending order, so on the live bank the run that already happened archived the OLDEST sections, which is the intended outcome. Worth hardening only as defence against a hand-edited out-of-order status.md.

backlog_items.title: checklist_v2.merge: on a duplicate stage the later block's name always wins, discarding richer v1 text
backlog_items.rationale: [slice B, reviewer line 'checklist_v2.py:156'] Confirmed at line 157: `Stage(n, st.done or prev.done, st.name or prev.name)` — the later non-empty name replaces the earlier one, and the v1 branch at lines 99-100 deliberately harvests the richer item text as the name, so a terser v2 duplicate downstream erases it. Non-blocking against AGR-043 as scoped by Stage 5: the load-bearing bit is preserved (done is OR'd, so a ✅ is never undone), the ⬜ set is preserved, this path never touches a closed plan's archived block (only live in-place folding), and cmd_apply writes `.checklist.md.bak.<ts>` before writing. The collision window is also narrow — mb-plan-sync's upsert calls rewrite(), which folds v1 and v2 into one block, so mixed state for one plan does not survive a sync.

backlog_items.title: checklist cap resolver accepts 0, silently disabling the documented hard cap
backlog_items.rationale: [slice B, reviewer line 'mb-checklist-prune.sh:64'] Confirmed: line 74's `case "$raw" in ''|*[!0-9]*)` treats '0' as valid, and cmd_apply in scripts/mb-checklist-v2.py:120/130 guards both the header rewrite and the exit-3 report behind `args.cap > 0`, so MB_CHECKLIST_MAX_LINES=0 turns the cap off with no diagnostic. Non-blocking: it is an undocumented off-switch reachable only by deliberately configuring 0, it removes a guard rather than destroying data, and the Stop hook's own cap check (mb-core-cap.sh) resolves independently. Either make 0 a documented kill-switch or require a strictly positive integer.

backlog_items.title: references/coordination.md promises a tagged LIFT clears a legacy freeze; mb-coord.sh never lifts legacy freezes
backlog_items.rationale: [slice C, reviewer line 'mb-coord.sh:207'] The reviewer's blocker framing is DISCARDED and the doc half is kept. The code behaviour is a verified, recorded decision, not a defect: .memory-bank/progress.md 2026-09-10 ('Разрешённое противоречие плана') states legacy freezes are reported fail-safe and prose lifts are deliberately not parsed, and Stage 6's risk row plus the DoD ('активный FREEZE … в выводе есть') back it. The code is also structurally incapable of the doc's promise — an untagged entry gets scope "" (mb-coord.sh line ~190), so no tagged LIFT scope could ever match it. What IS wrong is the doc sentence 'Legacy freezes are never auto-lifted … clear one by appending a tagged `## LIFT · <date> · <scope>`': that mechanism does not exist, and a session following it will still see the freeze. Fix the sentence (re-issue the freeze tagged, then LIFT it), or make legacy scope derivable. Over-reporting a freeze costs one line; missing one costs a destructive git op.

backlog_items.title: agents/mb-manager.md actualize --strict: heading-only append verification and ambiguous 'ideas → backlog.md' clause
backlog_items.rationale: [slice C, reviewer line 'mb-manager.md:419'] Both halves check out textually: line 419 instructs `grep -qxF` of the block heading only, and the 'Raw ideas go to backlog.md … not into the archive blob' bullet sits under an unconditional 'every line … is in progress.md VERBATIM first'. Non-blocking: this is prose for an LLM subagent, not shipped code, so there is no reproducible defect; the adjacent bullet already routes the whole `## Open backlog` section into progress.md as a block, making the ideas copy additive rather than a replacement; and the deterministic gate (mb-core-cap.sh check) plus the locked append-only progress.md still apply. Already partly filed as I-190 in backlog.md ('контракт держится только прозой'). Tighten the verification wording to 'append and byte-verify the complete block' and make the backlog.md copy explicitly additional.

backlog_items.title: mb-core-cap-guard.sh ignores marker-creation failure, so an unwritable bank is nudged every Stop
backlog_items.rationale: [slice C, reviewer line 'mb-core-cap-guard.sh:156'] Confirmed: line 156 is `: > "$MARKER" 2>/dev/null || true` immediately before block(), so on an unwritable bank the once-per-session contract at lines 18-20 silently degrades. Non-blocking: the session cannot wedge, because line 109 allows unconditionally on stop_hook_active=true, which is exactly the host's re-entry after a block; the failure mode is a repeated nudge across separate Stops, plus an unwritable bank is already a degraded environment. The header's own 'fail-open everywhere except the cap itself' rule argues for allow-on-marker-failure; add the unwritable-marker case to hooks/tests/test_core_cap_guard.bats.

backlog_items.title: mb-core-cap.sh fix downgrades rotate failures to warnings and discards prune failures other than exit 3
backlog_items.rationale: [slice C, reviewer line 'mb-core-cap.sh:175'] Confirmed: line 170 pipes the rotate failure into `|| echo '[warn] …'`, and prune_rc is captured but only compared against 3, so an exit-1 prune is dropped and the documented exit 2 ('internal error') is unreachable from a helper crash. Non-blocking: the gate decision itself is still honest, because `_report` re-measures the files after the helpers run — a failed repair that leaves the bank over cap still yields exit 1, and one that leaves it under cap is a correct 'under cap' answer. What is lost is the diagnostic that the repair failed, not the correctness of the cap verdict. Propagate helper runtime failures as exit 2 while keeping the exit-3 passthrough.

backlog_items.title: mb-coord.sh active: --tail N output has no byte bound (duplicate of I-189)
backlog_items.rationale: [slice C, reviewer line 'mb-coord.sh:232'] Accurate — the tail is emitted verbatim with no cap. Already filed: I-189 exists in .memory-bank/backlog.md (line ~1128, 'верхняя граница вывода не гарантирована — дословный хвост --tail N растёт'), raised by the /mb verify run before this review. Non-blocking: Stage 6's DoD is a measured budget on the live board and it reproduces today at 3678 B ≤ 4096; a single oversized tail entry is a possible future regression, not a present one. Record as a duplicate rather than a second item.

backlog_items.title: mb-coord.sh legacy-freeze heuristic requires a `**` somewhere on the line, not around the marker itself
backlog_items.rationale: [slice C, reviewer line 'mb-coord.sh:193'] Confirmed: the predicate is `'**' in ln and FREEZE_MARKER_RE.search(ln)`, so `**Note:** the prior FREEZE REQUEST is obsolete` would register. Non-blocking: it errs toward over-reporting, which is the recorded fail-safe direction, and the implementer's narrowing was validated empirically — progress.md 2026-09-10 records the verifier sweeping the whole live board for `freeze|заморож|⚠️` and confirming no false positive and no lost declaration, and the same entry already logs the exact-scope matching as a documented coarseness. Tighten to a bold span with a negative test when convenient.

backlog_items.title: test_core_cap.bats rotation fixture is dated ascending, the inverse of the real status.md convention
backlog_items.rationale: [slice C, reviewer line 'test_core_cap.bats:169'] DISCARDED as stated, kept as a realism note. The reviewer says the test 'contradicts the documented requirement to retain the newest three', but no such requirement exists: Stage 4 specifies 'сверх первых N' and mb-status-rotate.sh:9 documents first-N-in-file-order, and the test's own comment at line 166 says so. Applying the reviewer's fix as framed would make the test assert the opposite of the specification. The genuine residue is narrow: the fixture runs 2026-09-01→09-06 ascending while the real bank is newest-first (verified on `git show 364164a:.memory-bank/status.md`), so the test exercises the right code path on an unrealistic file. Reorder the fixture descending; the assertions then read naturally and still pass.

backlog_items.title: Full test battery is not green; Sprint 1's Gate wording requires tests_pass: true
backlog_items.rationale: Raised by the judge, not a reviewer. The plan's Gate (line 291) demands `mb-test-run.sh --out json` → tests_pass: true, and the recorded manual run was pytest 11 failed / bats 24 failed. Non-blocking for THIS sprint: every failure was attributed to files the range never touched, and the eight sprint-owned suites are green on re-run here — `bats tests/bats/test_status_rotate.bats test_mb_coord.bats test_core_cap.bats test_context_budget.bats test_plan_sync_v2.bats test_plan_done_v2.bats test_work_checkbox_v2.bats hooks/tests/test_core_cap_guard.bats` produced zero `not ok`. Blocking a closed sprint on pre-existing failures in unrelated code would move the goalposts onto someone else's scope. Track the pre-existing red battery as its own item so 'tests_pass: true' stops being a gate nobody can satisfy. (pytest is not installed in this judge's sandbox, so the pytest half rests on the verifier's evidence, not my own re-run.)
